effective.context:
Logos Blockchain is a Rust workspace (edition 2024, toolchain 1.99.0 pinned in rust-toolchain.toml, Cargo.lock committed). Package names carry a `logos-blockchain-` prefix the directory names lack; the `name` field of each crate's Cargo.toml is authoritative. The audited ref is the release tag 0.3.0 (commit 1da2d9d69a80452cf6b5d0e68304762d510c8a6c); record the resolved commit in the report. The specification in the prompt is the LIP as published in the logos-lips repository at commit fddc2c1 (the 2026-10-08 Bedrock snapshot).

Where the specification lives in the code:
- services/chain/chain-leader/src (package `logos-blockchain-chain-leader-service`): the block producer. lib.rs drives slot handling; leadership.rs finds a winning note and builds the leader proof; tx_selection.rs selects transactions from the mempool into the block body (ordering, gas and size limits, fee rules); mempool/ is the mempool adapter; blend.rs hands the block to Blend for dissemination; wallet.rs and kms.rs supply notes and keys; api.rs and relays.rs are service wiring.
- core/src/block/ (mod.rs, uncle.rs, deser.rs) and core/src/header/ (package `logos-blockchain-core`): the block and header types, body layout, content hash or root, uncle references, size and count limits.
- ledger/src/update.rs and src/lib.rs (package `logos-blockchain-ledger`): the validation side of the same rules, which a built block must satisfy.
- services/chain/chain-service/src/uncle.rs (package `logos-blockchain-chain-service`): uncle selection for a new block.
- Adjacent, outside the unit: the Mantle specification (transaction validation and execution, audited by its own briefs), the Cryptarchia Protocol LIP (header validation, audited by another brief), services/tx-service (the mempool).

Running tests: the gate runs the unit's packages with cargo-nextest, which is what CI uses (`.github/workflows/code-check.yml` runs the whole workspace that way; the whole workspace is too large for this container, so the gate is narrowed to the unit). `cargo nextest run --locked -p <package> --all-features` runs one package; `cargo test --locked -p <package> --all-features -- <filter>` works too. `.config/nextest.toml` marks a unit test slow after 30 s and kills it after 2 min. ZK proof dependencies come as prebuilt circuit crates (`lbc-*-sys` with the `prebuilt` feature) and the verifier links rapidsnark statically, so the first build compiles C++ and takes a while; nothing needs a running node, docker, or downloaded circuit files. New proof tests go in the owning crate's tests/ directory or as a `#[cfg(test)]` module file under src/ named by finding id; services/chain/chain-service/src/tests/ and core/src/mantle/fixtures/ show how blocks are built in tests. Treat code comments that cite a spec paragraph as claims to check.
